# Project Context

## Goal
Understand this repository as a design research and experimentation space focused on AI-augmented interface generation from an existing design system.

## Main challenge
The project investigates how AI can help designers and non-designers create high-quality interfaces faster, while remaining faithful to an existing design system and producing usable documentation for development.

## Reformulated problem statement
How can an AI-assisted workflow help teams move toward a “design for AI” practice by reusing an existing design system to generate interfaces, improve consistency, and strengthen handoff to developers?

## Important context
- The initial experimentation is centered around GitHub Copilot and related AI coding/design workflows.
- The design system exists in Figma and is used as the main source of UI truth.
- The expected result is not rough ideation only, but operational UI generation with strong structure and quality control.
- The long-term goal is an augmented AI interface where the designer provides inputs, constraints, and intent, and the system handles generation, checking, and documentation support.

## Use case 1
A person who is not a designer wants to create a digital interface quickly for a project.
The client already has a design system in Figma, including components, variables, and templates.
The user has supporting material such as documentation, sketches, and structured needs.
The deadline is short, so the user wants to delegate much of the interface creation to AI while keeping the result visually robust and close to high fidelity.

## Next steps context
- Compare workflow without AI vs with AI.
- Set up Copilot and related tooling.
- Use a shared VS Code project.
- Document repeatable steps.
- Build templates and instructions.
- Explore accessibility, eco-design, and design system checking.
- Improve handoff between design and front-end.
